extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants/owners and their attorneys/agents who must file a terminal disclaimer to overcome a double patenting rejection
extracted.subtask_description: Filling and submitting the USPTO terminal disclaimer (PTO/SB/26) to obviate a double patenting rejection over a prior patent, including required language, signatures, fee, and privacy/disclosure notices. Covers who may sign, fee/payment instructions, statutory/regulatory citations, and routine uses of the information provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer language — disclaimer of terminal part of statutory term
rubrics_metrics.description: "The owner . . . hereby disclaims, except as provided below, the terminal part of the statutory term of any patent granted on the instant application which would extend beyond the expiration date of the full statutory term prior patent No. __________________ as the term of said prior patent is defined in 35 U.S.C. 154 and 173, and as the term of said prior patent is presently shortened by any terminal disclaimer."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core declaratory language that must appear: identification of the owner, identification of the prior patent number, citation to 35 U.S.C. 154 and 173, and reference to any present shortening by an earlier terminal disclaimer. Include the optional docket/application identifiers as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceability limited to common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: "The owner hereby agrees that any patent so granted on the instant application shall be enforceable only for and during such period that it and the prior patent are commonly owned."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declares that the patent resulting from the application will be enforceable only while commonly owned with the referenced prior patent; this limitation is an express condition of the terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement runs with patent and binds successors/assigns
rubrics_metrics.description: "This agreement runs with any patent granted on the instant application and is binding upon the grantee, its successors or assigns."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that the disclaimer is attached to the patent and continues to bind future owners or assignees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to the disclaimer (situations where owner does not disclaim the terminal part)
rubrics_metrics.description: "In making the above disclaimer, the owner does not disclaim the terminal part of the term of any patent granted on the instant application that would extend to the expiration date of the full statutory term ... in the event that said prior patent later: expires for failure to pay a maintenance fee; is held unenforceable; is found invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction; is statutorily disclaimed in whole or terminally disclaimed under 37 CFR 1.321; has all claims canceled by a reexamination certificate; is reissued; or is in any manner terminated prior to the expiration of its full statutory term as presently shortened by any terminal disclaimer."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of seven specific events that, if later occurring to the prior patent, mean the terminal disclaimer will not bar extension of term to the full statutory expiration. The form requires these exceptions to be explicitly acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature/authority when signing for a business or organization (box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: "For submissions on behalf of a business/organization ... the undersigned is empowered to act on behalf of the business/organization. I hereby declare that all statements made herein of my own knowledge are true and that all statements made on information and belief are believed to be true; and further that these statements were made with the knowledge that willful false statements ... are punishable by fine or imprisonment, or both, under Section 1001 of Title 18 of the United States Code ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an organizational representative signs, they must assert authority to act for the organization and make the statutory declaration under penalty of law (18 U.S.C. §1001). Provide signature, date, typed/printed name, and telephone number as shown on the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature/authority when signing as attorney or agent of record (box 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The undersigned is an attorney or agent of record. Reg. No.___________________"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an attorney or registered agent signs, include their registration number and the same signature/date/printed name/telephone information. Either box 1 or 2 must be checked, as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer fee requirement (37 CFR 1.20(d)) and payment instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Terminal disclaimer fee under 37 CFR 1.20(d) included. Provide credit card information and authorization on PTO-2038. WARNING: Information on this form may become public. Credit card information should not [be included on this form]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fee per 37 CFR 1.20(d) must accompany the terminal disclaimer. Do not include credit card details on this form; instead use PTO-2038 for credit card authorization. Be aware the form may become public, so avoid including sensitive payment data on it. Follow PTO payment/submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement under 37 CFR 3.73(b) required if signed by assignee; certification form reference
rubrics_metrics.description: "*Statement under 37 CFR 3.73(b) is required if terminal disclaimer is signed by the assignee (owner). Form PTO/SB/96 may be used for making this certification. See MPEP § 324."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the assignee (rather than the original applicant) signs the terminal disclaimer, a certification under 37 CFR 3.73(b) is required. Use PTO/SB/96 to make that certification and consult MPEP §324 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory authority for collecting the information and confidentiality rules (37 CFR 1.321 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: "This collection of information is required by 37 CFR 1.321. ... Confidentiality is governed by 35 U.S.C. 122 and 37 CFR 1.11 and 1.14."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the terminal disclaimer is mandatory under 37 CFR 1.321 to obtain or retain the benefit (processing of the application). Confidentiality and release of records are governed by the cited statutes/regulations; applicants should follow the mailing and submission instructions on the form (send to Commissioner for Patents, etc.). Includes an estimated completion time (12 minutes) and where to send comments about paperwork burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act: authority, voluntariness, purpose, and consequence of not furnishing information
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Privacy Act of 1974 ... advises that: (1) the general authority for the collection of this information is 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(2); (2) furnishing of the information solicited is voluntary; and (3) the principal purpose for which the information is used by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office is to process and/or examine your submission related to a patent application or patent. If you do not furnish the requested information, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office may not be able to process and/or examine your submission, which may result in termination of proceedings or abandonment of the application or expiration of the patent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains statutory authority, that providing the information is voluntary but may have adverse consequences if omitted (e.g., abandonment), and the purpose for which USPTO uses the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use 1: Confidential treatment and possible DOJ disclosure for FOIA determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: "The information on this form will be treated confidentially to the extent allowed under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552) and the Privacy Act (5 U.S.C 552a). Records from this system of records may be disclosed to the Department of Justice to determine whether disclosure of these records is required by the Freedom of Information Act."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should understand that confidentiality is limited by FOIA/Privacy Act and that records may be shared with DOJ for FOIA-related determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use 2: Disclosure in course of litigation or settlement (courts, opposing counsel)
rubrics_metrics.description: "A record from this system of records may be disclosed, as a routine use, in the course of presenting evidence to a court, magistrate, or administrative tribunal, including disclosures to opposing counsel in the course of settlement negotiations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on the form may be disclosed during litigation, administrative proceedings, or settlement discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use 3: Disclosure to Members of Congress assisting constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: "A record in this system of records may be disclosed ... to a Member of Congress submitting a request involving an individual, to whom the record pertains, when the individual has requested assistance from the Member ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should know that records may be shared with Congressional offices at an applicant's request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use 4: Disclosure to contractors performing work for the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: "A record in this system of records may be disclosed ... to a contractor of the Agency having need for the information in order to perform a contract. Recipients of information shall be required to comply with the requirements of the Privacy Act ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party contractors who have a need to perform USPTO contracts may receive records, subject to Privacy Act compliance by the contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use 5: Disclosure to WIPO International Bureau for PCT international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: "A record related to an International Application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty in this system of records may be disclosed ... to the International Bureau of the World Intellectual Property Organization, pursuant to the Patent Cooperation Treaty."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the record pertains to a PCT international application, it may be shared with WIPO's IB under the PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use 6: Disclosure to other federal agencies for national security or atomic energy review
rubrics_metrics.description: "A record in this system of records may be disclosed ... to another federal agency for purposes of National Security review (35 U.S.C. 181) and for review pursuant to the Atomic Energy Act (42 U.S.C. 218(c))."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information may be provided to other agencies for statutory national security or atomic energy reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use 7: Disclosure to GSA during records inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: "A record from this system of records may be disclosed ... to the Administrator, General Services, or his/her designee, during an inspection of records conducted by GSA ... Such disclosure shall not be used to make determinations about individuals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The GSA may inspect records for records-management oversight; such disclosures are limited in purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use 8: Public disclosure after publication or issuance (or related abandoned applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: "A record from this system of records may be disclosed ... to the public after either publication of the application pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b) or issuance of a patent pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 151. Further, a record may be disclosed ... to the public if the record was filed in an application which became abandoned or in which the proceedings were terminated and which application is referenced by either a published application, an application open to public inspection or an issued patent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect that information on the form may become public once the application is published or a patent issues, and in certain related-abandonment circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use 9: Disclosure to law enforcement agencies if USPTO aware of violations
rubrics_metrics.description: "A record from this system of records may be disclosed ... to a Federal, State, or local law enforcement agency, if the USPTO becomes aware of a violation or potential violation of law or regulation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records may be shared with law enforcement if USPTO learns of possible legal violations; applicants should avoid including irrelevant sensitive information.
